title: tests: specify floor control move state scenarios
description:
Goal:
- Document the three floor-control move state scenarios to be tested.
- Analyze required DI/test setup inputs and dependencies.
Definition of Done:
- Scenarios are written as step-by-step flows for selection-rectangle + drag, clear selection on outside click, and single-position drag.
- Notes list DI registrations, view models, behaviors to activate, and required fakes.
Notes:
Scenarios:
1) Drag selection + move all:
   - Arrange: DI container; resolve GlobalStateModel, ApplicationStateMachine, FloorCanvasViewModel, ScenesPaneViewModel.
   - Build choreography (floor size, dancers, positions) and set on GlobalStateModel.
   - Activate ScenesPaneViewModel so LoadScenesBehavior maps SceneModel -> SceneViewModel and selects a scene.
   - Activate FloorCanvasViewModel behaviors.
   - Set InteractionMode=Move and apply MovePositionsStartedTrigger.
   - Drag a rectangle that intersects multiple positions (touch pressed/moved/released).
   - Drag one selected position by delta (touch pressed/moved/released).
   - Assert all selected positions moved by delta.
2) Clear selection on click outside:
   - Same setup through selection of multiple positions.
   - Touch press/release outside any position and outside floor bounds (or in bounds but no hit).
   - Assert SelectedPositions empty and SelectionRectangle null.
3) Single position drag:
   - Same setup, but touch press on a single position without selection rectangle.
   - Drag to new location; assert only that position moved by delta.

Setup analysis:
- Use ServiceCollection + AddMessagePipe + AddApplicationStateMachine.
- Register GlobalStateModel (no SettingsModel behaviors needed).
- Register fakes for IPreferences, IHapticFeedback, IVibration (IsSupported=false).
- Register FloorCanvasViewModel + IBehavior<FloorCanvasViewModel> = MovePositionsBehavior only.
- Register ScenesPaneViewModel + IBehavior<ScenesPaneViewModel> = LoadScenesBehavior only.
- Register SceneViewModel with empty behaviors list.
- Assign FloorCanvasViewModel.CanvasView to a new SKCanvasView and call UpdateFloorBounds with a known rect.
- Use SKTouchEventArgs constructors to drive TouchCommand on FloorCanvasViewModel.
